kurz: Tender means: the fibres separate easily. There are two ways to get there, depending on the cut.
bild_im_kopf: Two kinds of lock: some open with a light turn (cook a tender cut briefly), others only open with patience (braise the connective tissue).
bedeutung: Two things make meat tough: tightly contracted muscle fibres and undissolved connective tissue. Tender cuts have little connective tissue and stay tender if you do not overcook them. Cuts with lots of connective tissue only turn tender once it dissolves into gelatine over hours.
was_passiert: Frying a braising cut quickly or braising a fillet is taking the wrong path. Cutting across the grain makes the fibres short and every bite more tender.
faustregeln: Quick frying only for tender cuts.
Cook braising cuts long and low.

praxis.text: Fillet quick and pink; shoulder or shin braised for hours.
In baking, tender means little [[glutenbildung|gluten network]]. Mix briefly; fat helps.
